{{nihongo|'''Futamata Shrine'''|二俣神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|Q71707|qid=Q71707}}{{ill|Iwaki, Fukushima|Q274384|qid=Q274384}}{{ill|Ogawa-machi Shimogawa|Q128847384|qid=Q128847384}}. It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=shikinaisha (minor shrine)}}, and under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=former shrine rank system}} it was classified as a gōsha. {{nihongo|'''Futamata Shrine'''|二俣神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mutsu Province]].

== History ==
According to shrine tradition, it was established by enshrinement in the first year of {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} ({{ill|860|Q24714|qid=Q24714}}). In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, it is listed as one of the seven shrines of {{ill|Iwaki district|Q11585428|qid=Q11585428|lt=Iwaki District}}, ranked as a minor shrine.

In the second year of {{ill|1289|Q5551|qid=Q5551}} ({{ill|1289|Q5551|qid=Q5551}}), {{ill|Ogawa Muneyoshi|Q132431591|qid=Q132431591}} (also known as Ogawa Yoshitsuna), the second son of {{ill|Satake Yoshitane|Q60990135|qid=Q60990135}}, who had advanced into this region, restored the main shrine.

== From the Edo period onward ==
It is said that the shrine originally stood at the site of Kawakami Hachimangū, located a little over 1 km northwest of the present location. However, due to frequent flood damage, it was relocated to its current site in the second year of {{ill|Tenna|Q1145289|qid=Q1145289|lt=Tenna}} ({{ill|1682|Q7648|qid=Q7648}}) by {{ill|Iwakitaira Domain|Q843782|qid=Q843782}} lord {{ill|Naitō Yoshimune|Q8514975|qid=Q8514975}}. In the 11th year of {{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}} ({{ill|1698|Q7706|qid=Q7706}}), shrine building repairs were carried out by domain lord {{ill|Naitō Yoshitaka|Q8514986|qid=Q8514986}}, and thereafter repairs continued under the patronage of successive domain lords.

In the fourth year of {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} ({{ill|1871|Q7746|qid=Q7746}}), it was ranked as a {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}, and in the seventh year of Meiji ({{ill|1874|Q7761|qid=Q7761}}) the present shrine buildings were constructed.

== Shrine grounds ==
Within the grounds is the '''Umenosaku tile kiln site''', where tiles were produced for the Natsui Haiji temple ruins (Iwaki City {{ill|Taira Shimogōe|Q128846875|qid=Q128846875}}). The Natsui Haiji temple was located downstream along the Natsui River, and it is thought that the tiles were loaded onto boats and transported down the river.

== Access ==
* {{ill|East Japan Railway Company|Q499071|qid=Q499071}} (JR East) {{ill|Ban'etsu East Line|Q807037|qid=Q807037}} (Yūyū Abukuma Line): 30 minutes on foot from either “{{ill|Akai Station|Q4700176|qid=Q4700176}}” or “{{ill|Ogawagō Station|Q7079855|qid=Q7079855}}” (the shrine is located almost midway between the two stations).
